text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri to meet Morocco's King Hassan today.
Hariri arrived in Morocco on Tuesday to discuss the stalled Middle East peace process.
- Former Hizbollah leader Sobhi Tufaili threatens to spread civil disobedience campaign to Beirut.
The radical Shi'ite cleric is urging residents of the Bekaa Valley to start a civil disobedience campaign on July 4 to pressure the government into easing poverty in the region.
- Differences between Lebanese political leaders heating up. Syrian mediation eases tensions.
- Malaysian automobiles to enter Lebanese market.
- Israel shelling of western Bekaa Valley damages houses and burns automobiles.
- Former parliament speaker presents proposal to make judiciary more independent.
- Parliamentary deputies' draft law calls on government to cancel decision to increase car import duties.
- Prime Minister Hariri says the peace process is in a crisis.
